data.body:
Premise VALIDATED against current main, with the seam located precisely.

`test_a_missing_epic_field_aborts_provisioning` stubs `/rest/api/2/field` to return a body carrying `Epic Name` but not `Epic Link`, so the readiness poll can only expire. It expires against the real production budget: `scripts/jira_dc_field_readiness.py:114` `FIELD_READY_BUDGET_S = 120.0`, polled at `FIELD_POLL_INTERVAL_S = 1.0` (line 95). `await_required_fields` (line 226) loops request -> `if monotonic() >= deadline: break` -> `sleep(interval)`, so the unit test performs ~120 stub reads and sleeps ~120 real seconds. That matches the filed 120.39-121.03s.

One correction to the ticket's framing, caught by plan review. The ticket says "the readiness API already accepts injected sleep and monotonic functions", which is true of `await_required_fields` — but the caller under test does NOT forward them. `_assert_project_capabilities` (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py:580-581`) computes `field_budget = _field_ready_timeout()` and passes `budget=` explicitly, so injection is unreachable from the test without changing a production signature. `_field_ready_timeout()` (line 157) reads `JIRA_DC_FIELD_READY_TIMEOUT` and only falls back to the module constant when it is unset — so monkeypatching `FIELD_READY_BUDGET_S` would ALSO have been silently defeated whenever that variable is set in the ambient environment. The env var is the one seam that is deterministic from the test, and `tests/unit/test_live_jira_dc_conftest.py:296` already uses it.
